subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `skills.load` source-disable contract for built-in personal/project agent skill roots, and what exact config shape should own it?
rationale: The issue is valid from source inspection, but OpenClaw policy sets a high bar for new config surface and the chosen shape becomes a public runtime/config contract.

options.title: Add typed source-disable list
options.body: Expose a default-empty `skills.load.disableSources` style list for known built-in source ids and apply it before discovery, watcher registration, and status/snapshot output.

options.title: Add narrow personal toggle
options.body: Expose only a boolean for `agents-skills-personal`, minimizing surface but likely requiring another option if project `.agents/skills` needs the same treatment later.

options.title: Keep current source model
options.body: Decline the new config surface and rely on per-skill disables, prompt limits, and skill organization, accepting that the source is always discovered.

recommendation.title: Add typed source-disable list
recommendation.body: Expose a default-empty `skills.load.disableSources` style list for known built-in source ids and apply it before discovery, watcher registration, and status/snapshot output.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows adjacent watcher and skills-loader work on this source family, making this the best available routing owner for the config/API decision.
